items.title: Silk traces found on 101 ancient Chinese ritual objects dating back 3,000 years
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Scientists studying 3,000-year-old objects from China's Sanxingdui archaeological site have found silk traces on 101 artefacts, including bronze masks, gold, jade and ivory objects. Published in the journal Antiquity, the study suggests that ancient Shu people used silk to wrap or cover objects during rituals. Researchers also identified red pigments and different weaving patterns, offering clues about ancient textile practices.

items.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current opens free soccer league for 120 children
items.author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
items.description: The Kansas City Current launched a free youth soccer league in July to help children overcome financial barriers to sports. The program provides 120 players aged 8 to 10 with uniforms, Nike cleats and equipment at no cost. Supported by community partners, the initiative also offers coach stipends and referee training for teenagers. The league aims to expand access, support local families and encourage greater participation, particularly among girls.

items.title: Texas jury finds stepson not adopted despite 1980 will calling him 'child'
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: In a complex Texas inheritance case, a stepson referred to as 'my child' in a will navigated a treacherous dispute following his father's passing. Despite his claims of informal adoption, the family remained unconvinced. Ultimately, the jury affirmed that no formal or informal adoption occurred. This outcome highlights the necessity of clear legal documentation in estate planning to avoid misunderstandings, particularly within blended families concerning rights to inheritance.

items.title: Steven Spielberg's $29.9m LA horse ranch disappears from property listings
items.author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
items.description: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg listed his Los Angeles ranch for $29.9 million but has now taken it off the market. He and his wife purchased the property in 1999 for $5.75 million, intending to create equestrian facilities. After facing opposition from local residents, their renovation plans were significantly reduced over the years. The ranch, known as Dogwood, features a main house with numerous upscale amenities and a 20,000-square-foot riding arena.

items.title: William Gilbert's 1600 book saying Earth is a magnet sells for Rs 58.5 lakh
items.author: TIMESOFINDIA.COM
items.description: William Gilbert's pivotal publication, De Magnete, emerged in 1600, marking a significant shift in the exploration of magnetism and electricity. It introduced key terms and experimental approaches that influenced future electrical studies. The concept of Earth as a colossal magnet was groundbreaking. Recently, a first edition fetched $61,440 at a Christie’s auction, highlighting its enduring significance and the continued fascination it holds in scientific discourse.
